correctness.rationale: Reid--Tai on the two heavy charts gives exactly \(0\le d=b-a\le r,\ 1\le a\le r+d\) in the canonical case and the strict inequalities in the terminal case. The standard weighted-projective volume is \((r+a+b)^{r+1}/(ab)\). For fixed \(d\), the logarithmic derivative has one positive zero, so the maximum on the allowed \(a\)-interval is at an endpoint; the submitted derivative calculations then make the outer endpoint monotone in \(d\), while the lower endpoint is strictly smaller except for the stated canonical \(r=2\) tie. I independently enumerated the exact rational feasible regions for \(2\le r\le40\), reproducing every formula and equality case; this is corroboration, not the infinite proof.
correctness.risk: The proof is specialized to ordinary \(\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\); no global bound over all weighted projective spaces follows.

final_claim: For \(X_{r,a,b}=\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\) with \(r\ge2\), the sharp canonical anticanonical-volume maximum is \(6^r r^{r-1}\), attained uniquely at \((a,b)=(2r,3r)\) for \(r\ge3\) and at \((1,3),(4,6)\) for \(r=2\); the sharp terminal maximum is \(64\) at \((1,1)\) for \(r=2\), and for \(r\ge3\) is \((6r-5)^{r+1}/(6(r-1)^2)\), attained uniquely at \((2r-2,3r-3)\).
limitations: Ordinary complex weighted projective spaces of the form \(\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\) only.
